category_title: Students experiencing sensory overload and avoidance behaviors due to trauma
minimal_context: Natasha arrives at the classroom and is asked to take out her textbook and assignment for the lesson.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please take your seat. We are starting the lesson, so take out your textbook and the assignment from yesterday.

STUDENT: I don't have my book. The hallways... the smells out there made me dizzy and weak... sick to my stomach almost.

TUTOR: We need the book for today's lesson. What about the assignment?

STUDENT: I only have part of it done. Everything is just cloudy upstairs today. It takes all my effort just remembering what room it is in and going.

TUTOR: Oh, Natasha, you chose to join us today. We expect you to be prepared when you do.

STUDENT: (Grabs her bag and turns to leave the classroom) I can't do this. When you say things like that, you just don't want to go back after that.

options.A: Provide external regulation to help the student start inhibiting the inappropriate urge to leave the classroom.
options.B: Allow the student to leave the classroom when struggling and do not make an issue of the forgotten textbook.
options.C: Adjust the classroom environment to reduce ambient noise while the student is in the room.
options.D: Provide a detailed instruction of each specific element required to complete the assignment in the classroom.
